newsitem.title: USA: Steps to take for job evaluations.
newsitem.headline: Steps to take for job evaluations.

text.p: Here are some tips to help make a negative job evaluation as productive as possible.

-- Sit down beforehand and think out what the aim of the performance appraisal is. "The aim is to help this person be more satisfied at work and produce more," said Joe Gibbons, a consultant with Towers Perrin in New York.
-- Try to get the employee involved with what you need to fix, not to point the finger at the person. Ask, 'What can we do better? What are your ideas?'
-- Enter the session aware of the employee's working conditions, including the amount of work, the resources and budget.

-- Try to understand why the person is performing poorly and address their skills and motivation. "If you take a development view as oppposed to a punitive view, you have a different conversation," consultant Charles Labig said.
-- Create an ability for employees to appeal negative job reviews through "a fair dispute resolution process," said sociologist John King of Baldwin-Wallace College in Berea, Ohio.
-- Give an employee a road map, something that says, 'We're not just going to criticise you, we're also going to help you improve.'
